facts.quote: About 0900, the Titan was released from the LARS and began its descent to the Titanic wreckage at a rate of 98 feet per minute (30 meters per minute).

facts.label: Dive number of the fatal (casualty) dive

facts.quote: OceanGate typically charged $250,000 for the Titanic experience — a steep jump in price from $105,129 it charged in 2021, according to the report.

findings.text: The Coast Guard board chair said the casualty and the loss of five lives was preventable.

OceanGate's failure to follow established engineering protocols for safety, testing and maintenance was the primary causal factor; Titan's design, certification, maintenance and inspection were all inadequate.
The Coast Guard cited a toxic workplace culture at OceanGate and a lack of a domestic and international framework for submersible operations.
For years OceanGate used intimidation tactics, allowances for scientific operations and its reputation to evade regulatory scrutiny, operating Titan outside established deep-sea protocols.

OceanGate failed to investigate known hull anomalies after its 2022 expedition, did no preventive maintenance and stored Titan uncovered outdoors over the winter; had Rush survived, the board would have recommended manslaughter charges.

notes: news.uscg.mil, news.usni.org and the report PDF on media.defense.gov returned 403 to this session, so the USCG figures come via ABC, NBC, NPR, Marine Log and CompositesWorld; the NTSB final report (MIR-25-36, dated 2025-10-02) was fetched directly and is official. Conflicts: Titanic depth 3,800 m (ABC, Coast Guard) vs 3,880 m (NTSB) vs 3,840 m dive depth (NTSB). Loss-of-contact depth 3,346 m (USCG via ABC) vs 'At 1047, while the Titan was at a depth of 11,032 feet (3,363 meters)' (NTSB). Debris distance: 500 m (NTSB, ABC) but the NTSB's own conversion reads '1,148 feet' (500 m is about 1,640 ft, likely a typo), and AP (adn.com) says 'about 330 yards off the bow'; use 500 m. Report length: 335 pages (ABC, Maritime Executive), 327 (NBC), 'over 300' (CBS, Marine Log), '300-page' (NPR); treat as doubtful or say 'more than 300 pages'. Build year: NTSB says the v2 pressure vessel was 'constructed in 2020' and 'Built in 2020' but elsewhere 'constructed ... in 2021'; Maritime Executive says 'Titan, built in 2021'; the bonding ran Nov 2020 - Jan 2021. The 17 recommendations figure was seen on Marine Log and CompositesWorld (both quoting the USCG release), not on the USCG page itself. Implosion time 1047 is local (Newfoundland daylight) time per NTSB; NBC quotes 10:47 a.m. Not found on a fetchable page: 2018 MTS letter signatory count, the 1,600 ft debris figure, and the 2019 USCG report; dropped. Extra available figures: NTSB says search found debris June 22 at 0940, Polar Prince called JRCC Halifax about 1855 (NBC says the Canadian Coast Guard was notified at 7:10 p.m.); 48 equipment issues in 2022 (ABC); stored about seven months outdoors (ABC via Yahoo); value about $4.2 million USD (NTSB). Also seen but left out to stay within 28: descent rate 30 m/min (NTSB), 'All good here' at about 2,274 m (ABC), 2021 price $105,129 (NBC), 70 equipment issues in 2021 (ABC).
